family.amstrad-series-5.description: Amstrad compact office desktops: PC5086, PC5286 and the extension to the 386SX with PC5386SX.
family.amstrad-series-5.history:
In September 1991, the press announced that Amstrad would introduce Series 5 that month at the Business Computing '91 show at Earl's Court, London. It was a range of office desktop PCs in a small case designed to take up little desk space; the August brochure called it "a series of small footprint, professional PC's".

The series started with two models. The PC5086 had an 8086 at 8 MHz and 640 KB of memory, with one or two 3.5-inch floppy drives or a 40 MB hard disk. The PC5286 stepped up to an 80286 at 16 MHz with 1 MB, expandable to 2 or 4 MB, and was sold with a floppy drive alone or with a 40 MB IDE disk. Both shared VGA graphics, a PS/2-style keyboard and mouse, MS-DOS 3.3 and Counterpoint, a graphical interface from Oberwerk for starting programs and managing files with the mouse instead of the command line. The announced entry price was £400.

That same month Amstrad offered the PC5286 as a Games Pack: the computer with an AdLib-compatible sound card, a joystick, speakers and several games, including Links, F-15 Strike Eagle II and Prince of Persia. It was the same office machine, prepared for use at home.

In September 1991, Science & Vie Micro announced a possible extension to the family with the PC5386, based on a 16 MHz 386SX and without a launch date. Lawson included it in his list of Amstrad PCs, and two Australian owners documented PC5386SX and PC5386SXHD machines in 1999 and 2000. The secondary system-cfg sheet specifies 20 MHz: the discrepancy remains open. The PC5086 and PC5286 brochure states British design and manufacture in Taiwan, Korea or the United Kingdom; it does not establish an OEM for the PC5386SX.

family.amstrad-series-5.table.note: PC5086 and PC5286 appear in the 1991 presentation; Games Pack is a PC5286 configuration. PC5386SX has an announcement and owner accounts, but its sale date and the 16/20 MHz discrepancy remain unresolved.
